slides.1.title: Touriga Nacional — The Soul Grape of Portugal
slides.1.html:
Touriga Nacional is Portugal's most important red grape, known as the "soul" of Portuguese wine. Native to the Dão region, it is now widely planted in the Douro, Alentejo and elsewhere.

🎨 Appearance

  • Colour: extremely deep purple-black, opaque, with a touch of ruby at the rim
  • High viscosity, with pronounced tears

👃 Aromas (Key to Blind Tasting)

  • Primary aromas: violet (the single most important identifier!), blueberry, blackberry, blackcurrant
  • Secondary aromas: none (floral and fruit notes dominate when young)
  • Tertiary aromas (with age): cedar, tobacco, liquorice, chocolate

👅 Palate

  • High acidity and high tannin (but fine-grained), robust structure
  • Medium to high alcohol, full body
  • Extremely long finish, up to 30+ seconds (in top vintages)
slides.2.title: Syrah in Portugal vs. Baga — Telling Them Apart
slides.2.html:
🌶️ Syrah (Portugal, especially Douro/Alentejo)

  • Appearance: deep purple-black, slightly lighter than Touriga Nacional
  • Aroma: black pepper (the strongest identifier!), smoke, olive, lavender, black olive
  • Palate: smooth tannins, medium to high acidity, full body; warmer and rounder than French Syrah
  • Ageing: cedar, leather, bacon fat (typical Rhône character)

🍒 Baga (Bairrada)

  • Appearance: medium-depth red (paler than the other two), with a garnet rim
  • Aroma: red berries (strawberry, sour cherry), rose petal, earthiness, a slight green-stalk note
  • Palate: very high acidity (comparable to Nebbiolo/Sangiovese), high, grippy tannins, light body
  • Risk of misjudgement: very tight and astringent when young, easily mistaken for a fault. Silky and captivating with age

🧠 Blind Tasting Memory Aid

Touriga = Violet | Syrah = Pepper | Baga = Acid (high acidity)

slides.4.question: In blind tasting, which aroma best helps identify Touriga Nacional?
slides.4.explanation: Violet is the most distinctive identifier of Touriga Nacional and is extremely rare among major grape varieties. Together with deep purple colour and high tannin, it forms the golden triangle for identifying Touriga Nacional.
slides.5.question: Why is Baga most often misjudged in blind tastings?
slides.5.options.2: Its very high acidity and astringency when young are often mistaken for faults
slides.5.explanation: Baga is one of the grapes with the highest acidity and tannin in the world. When young it is very tight and astringent, and inexperienced tasters easily mistake this for a quality problem. In fact it is a structural trait that means Baga needs ageing to show its charm.
